findings.issue: Repeatedly ran `pkill -f 'node .output/server/index.mjs'` inside the same bash command as builds/tests/starts; the pattern matches the invoking shell's own command line, SIGTERMs it (exit 143), and the agent misattributed this to 'the harness killing lingering processes' across ~9 calls
findings.suggestion: Kill by port or PID (e.g. `lsof -t -i:3100 | xargs -r kill`) or use a pattern that can't match the pkill command itself; diagnose one 143 once and the whole class disappears

findings.issue: Production SSR returned 'Not found' for all name-based routes for several minutes; the agent added logging, could not reproduce, and moved on without a root cause — an unreproduced-then-vanished failure mode was shipped
findings.suggestion: Reproduce with the logging build first (the rebuild that 'fixed' it may have masked a real intermittent bug, e.g. a stale process on the port serving old code); at minimum document the hypothesis set and what was ruled out

findings.issue: Zero web searches/fetches and zero skill/doc reads for Nuxt; relied entirely on training-data knowledge of Nuxt 4 (the E1001 runtime-context error and the Vue SFC export limitation were both discoverable in docs)
findings.suggestion: When using a specific framework version, check the current docs for the APIs in play (useAsyncData context rules, script-setup constraints) before writing the data layer

findings.issue: Two edit calls failed because the agent 'remembered' file content (a tokens.css typo, a PokemonCard typo) that wasn't actually there — trusting truncated write echoes over fresh reads
findings.suggestion: Re-read (or grep) the target region before editing whenever the belief comes from a previous write's preview rather than a read

findings.issue: Debug instrumentation (console.error in fetchRecord) added during the transient-failure investigation remains in the shipped data layer, gated to non-404 errors
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is, but consider a structured logger or removing it now that the investigation is over

findings.issue: Never ran a typecheck or dev-server compile until the first production build, despite writing TypeScript SFCs and pre-empting one SFC error by inspection
findings.suggestion: Run `nuxt typecheck` (or at least the dev-server compile) right after scaffolding components to catch SFC/TS issues before wiring pages

summary: A well-planned, thoroughly verified session: it front-loaded spec/test/data/design analysis, passed the full suite on the first run, and re-verified both visuals and tests after every change. Weaknesses are operational rather than conceptual — repeated self-terminating shell commands, a never-root-caused transient SSR failure, and total reliance on training-data Nuxt knowledge instead of docs. The output quality is high; the process friction cost maybe a dozen of the 103 turns.
